## Key Updates: Version 2.2026 {.smaller}

**GAST-F (Perioperative Therapy)** — FLOT + Durvalumab changes:

- Sub-bullets added: For **clinical node negative** tumor
- Sub-bullet added: For **PD-L1 CPS <1 or TAP <1%** (category 2B)
- Sub-bullet added: For **diffuse type** (category 2B)
- Footnote revised: In the **MATTERHORN trial**, diffuse type gastric/EGJ adenocarcinoma showed **no event-free overall survival advantage** when durvalumab was added to FLOT

**Reference Added:** Tabernero J, et al. *Annals of Oncology* 2025;36:S1623-S1624

---

## Key Updates: Version 1.2026 (Selected) {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**GAST-1 / GAST-2**

- HER2 (ERBB2) testing revised: for **advanced/metastatic** disease documented or suspected
- Added bullet: **Assess for distress**
- Superficial vs. deep pT1b defined: ≤500 μm = superficial; >500 μm = deep

**GAST-B (Biomarkers)**

- MSI testing: now by **PCR or NGS**; MMR by IHC
- PD-L1: companion diagnostic required; CLIA-approved labs only
- TAP score and CPS: high concordance — **interchangeable** for tislelizumab and durvalumab
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**GAST-F (Systemic Therapy)**

- **Dostarlimab-gxly** added for MSI-H/dMMR neoadjuvant therapy
- **Fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki** upgraded to **category 1** (2nd-line HER2+)
- Subcutaneous pembrolizumab (with berahyaluronidase alfa-pmph) may substitute IV pembrolizumab
- Subcutaneous nivolumab (with hyaluronidase-nvhy) may substitute IV nivolumab for monotherapy

**GAST-G** — Heading revised: "Supportive Care"
:::
::::

# Overview & Epidemiology {background-color="#1a5276"}

---

## Global Epidemiology of Gastric Cancer {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
**Global Burden (2022)**

- **>968,000 new cases** worldwide
- **~660,000 deaths** annually
- **5th most frequent** cancer globally
- **5th leading cause** of cancer-related death globally
- 15–20 fold difference between high and low-incidence regions

**Geographic Hotspots**

- Northeast Asia (Japan, Korea, China)
- South and Central America
- Eastern Europe

**United States (2025 Estimates)**

- 30,300 new diagnoses expected
- 10,780 projected deaths
- 15th most common cancer; 15th leading cancer death cause
:::
::: {.column width="40%"}
**Incidence Trends**

- Declining in Western countries and North America — driven by:
  - Improved food preservation
  - Clean water access
  - H. pylori eradication
  - Dietary changes

- **Rising**: Early-onset gastric cancer in the U.S. and Western countries

- **Persistently high**: Distal stomach tumors in low/middle-income countries

> In Japan and South Korea, widespread population screening leads to **early detection** and improved outcomes
:::
::::

---

## Histology & Pathogenesis {.smaller}

**>95% of gastric cancers are adenocarcinomas**

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Diffuse Type (Lauren Classification)**

- Poorly differentiated, discohesive tumor cells
- Signet-ring or non-signet-ring morphology
- Desmoplastic stroma
- More prevalent in **low-risk areas**
- Associated with heritable (CDH1) mutations
- **Increasing incidence** in proximal stomach
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Intestinal Type**

- Tubular/glandular pattern
- Scattered goblet cells
- More common in **high-risk areas**
- Related to environmental factors:
  - H. pylori infection
  - Tobacco smoking
  - High salt diet
  - Other dietary factors
- **Declining incidence** in developed countries
:::
::::

> **Note:** Role of alcohol is debated; heavy use associated with non-cardia gastric cancer

---

## Hereditary Cancer Predisposition Syndromes {.smaller}

**1–3% of gastric cancers** are associated with inherited syndromes

| Syndrome | Gene | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Hereditary Diffuse Gastric Cancer (HDGC)** | CDH1 | Most well-characterized; prophylactic total gastrectomy may be indicated |
| **Lynch Syndrome** | MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2 | Associated with MSI-H/dMMR tumors |
| **Juvenile Polyposis Syndrome** | SMAD4, BMPR1A | GI polyps; elevated gastric cancer risk |
| **Familial Adenomatous Polyposis (FAP)** | APC | Gastric fundic gland polyps; increased risk |

> See NCCN Guidelines for Genetic/Familial High-Risk Assessment: Colorectal, Endometrial, and Gastric for full assessment criteria

# Staging {background-color="#1a5276"}

---

## AJCC TNM Staging — T Classification (8th Ed., 2017) {.smaller}

| Category | Definition |
|---|---|
| **TX** | Primary tumor cannot be assessed |
| **T0** | No evidence of primary tumor |
| **Tis** | Carcinoma in situ: intraepithelial tumor, high-grade dysplasia |
| **T1** | Tumor invades lamina propria, muscularis mucosae, or submucosa |
| **T1a** | Tumor invades lamina propria or muscularis mucosae |
| **T1b** | Tumor invades submucosa |
| **T2** | Tumor invades muscularis propria |
| **T3** | Tumor penetrates subserosal connective tissue, no visceral peritoneum invasion |
| **T4a** | Tumor invades serosa (visceral peritoneum) |
| **T4b** | Tumor invades adjacent structures/organs |

> T4b adjacent structures: spleen, transverse colon, liver, diaphragm, pancreas, abdominal wall, adrenal gland, kidney, small intestine, retroperitoneum

---

## AJCC TNM Staging — N, M, G Classification {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
**N — Regional Lymph Nodes**

| Category | Definition |
|---|---|
| NX | Cannot be assessed |
| N0 | No regional LN metastasis |
| N1 | Metastasis in 1–2 LNs |
| N2 | Metastasis in 3–6 LNs |
| N3a | Metastasis in 7–15 LNs |
| N3b | Metastasis in ≥16 LNs |

**M — Distant Metastasis**

| Category | Definition |
|---|---|
| M0 | No distant metastasis |
| M1 | Distant metastasis |
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
**G — Histologic Grade**

| Grade | Description |
|---|---|
| GX | Cannot be assessed |
| G1 | Well differentiated |
| G2 | Moderately differentiated |
| G3 | Poorly differentiated / undifferentiated |

**Submucosal Invasion (pT1b)**

| Type | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Superficial** pT1b | ≤500 μm invasion of submucosa |
| **Deep** pT1b | >500 μm invasion of submucosa |

> This distinction is crucial for staging accuracy and management decisions (EUS is **not reliable** for predicting superficial vs. deep submucosal invasion — ER recommended for accurate staging)
:::
::::

---

## AJCC Stage Groupings — Clinical (cTNM) {.smaller}

| Stage | cT | cN | M |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Stage 0** | Tis | N0 | M0 |
| **Stage I** | T1 | N0 | M0 |
| **Stage I** | T2 | N0 | M0 |
| **Stage IIA** | T1–T2 | N1, N2, N3 | M0 |
| **Stage IIB** | T3 | N0 | M0 |
| **Stage IIB** | T4a | N0 | M0 |
| **Stage III** | T3–T4a | N1, N2, N3 | M0 |
| **Stage IVA** | T4b | Any N | M0 |
| **Stage IVB** | Any T | Any N | M1 |

---

## AJCC Stage Groupings — Pathologic (pTNM) {.smaller}

| Stage | pT | pN | M |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Stage 0** | Tis | N0 | M0 |
| **Stage IA** | T1 | N0 | M0 |
| **Stage IB** | T1/T2 | N1/N0 | M0 |
| **Stage IIA** | T1–T3 | N0–N2 | M0 |
| **Stage IIB** | T1–T4a | N0–N3a | M0 |
| **Stage IIIA** | T2–T4b | N0–N3a | M0 |
| **Stage IIIB** | T1–T4b | N0–N2 | M0 |
| **Stage IIIC** | T3–T4b | N3a–N3b | M0 |
| **Stage IV** | Any T | Any N | M1 |

**Post-Neoadjuvant (ypTNM) — 4 broad stages: I, II, III, IV**

# Initial Workup {background-color="#1a5276"}

---

## GAST-1: Workup at Presentation {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
**Required Workup**

- History & Physical (H&P)
- Esophagogastroduodenoscopy (**EGD**) with biopsy
- CT chest/abdomen/pelvis with oral and IV contrast
- **FDG-PET/CT** (skull base to mid-thigh) for locally advanced or metastatic disease (may not be appropriate for T1)
- CBC and comprehensive chemistry profile
- **EUS** — recommended if early-stage disease suspected or early vs. locally advanced needs determination
- **Endoscopic resection (ER)** — essential for accurate staging of T1a or T1b

**Biomarker Testing (All Patients)**

- Universal MSI testing (PCR/NGS) or MMR by IHC
- Universal PD-L1 testing (IHC)
- HER2 (ERBB2) testing if advanced/metastatic disease documented or suspected
- CLDN18.2 testing if advanced/metastatic suspected
- NGS should be considered
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
**Additional Workup**

- Biopsy of metastatic disease (as indicated)
- Siewert category assessment
- Nutritional assessment and counseling
- Smoking cessation advice and pharmacotherapy
- Screen for family history of gastric cancer
- Test for H. pylori — eradicate if positive in early gastric cancer; recommend testing of close family members
- **Assess for distress** (NCCN Distress Thermometer)

**Clinical Stage Groups**

| Stage | Description |
|---|---|
| cTis / cT1a | Localized |
| cT1b–cT4a, cM0 | Locoregional |
| Stage IV, cM1 | Metastatic |
:::
::::

---

## GAST-1: Footnotes & Key Principles {.smaller}

**Siewert Classification (EGJ Tumors)**

| Type | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Type I** | Adenocarcinoma of distal esophagus; epicenter 1–5 cm above EGJ |
| **Type II** | True carcinoma of cardia; epicenter within 1 cm above and 2 cm below EGJ |
| **Type III** | Subcardial carcinoma; epicenter 2–5 cm below EGJ |

- **Siewert I & II** → Manage per NCCN Guidelines for Esophageal and EGJ Cancers
- **Siewert III** → Manage per NCCN Guidelines for Gastric Cancer (may need additional esophageal resection for margins)

**EUS Note:**
- EUS is **not reliable** for predicting superficial or deep submucosal invasion
- Endoscopic resection recommended for accurate staging
- Superficial pT1b defined as ≤500 μm; deep pT1b as >500 μm

# Multidisciplinary Review & Primary Treatment {background-color="#1a5276"}

---

## GAST-2: Primary Treatment Pathways {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**cTis / cT1a or Superficial cT1b**

- *Nonsurgical candidate* → **Endoscopic Resection (ER)** → Endoscopic surveillance
- *Medically fit* → **ER or Surgery** → Surgical outcomes (GAST-4)

**Deep cT1b**

- *Medically fit, potentially resectable* → **Surgery** → GAST-4

**cT2 or higher, Any N (potentially resectable)**

- Surgery alone
- **Perioperative systemic therapy** (category 1)
- Consider neoadjuvant/perioperative ICI if MSI-H/dMMR
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Surgically Unresectable Locoregional (cM0)**

- *Medically fit* → **Chemoradiation or Systemic therapy** → GAST-6 Post-Treatment Assessment

**Nonsurgical Candidate (Locoregional)**

- **Palliative Management (GAST-9)**

**Metastatic Disease (cM1)**

- **Palliative Management (GAST-9)**

> Surgery as primary therapy appropriate for ≥T1b cancer, actively bleeding cancer, or when postoperative therapy preferred (footnote q)
:::
::::

---

## GAST-3: Response Assessment {.smaller}

**For Patients Who Are Medically Fit**

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**After Perioperative Systemic Therapy (Category 1)**

Imaging assessment:
- Chest/abdomen/pelvis CT with oral and IV contrast
- FDG-PET/CT as clinically indicated

**Outcomes:**

| Finding | Management |
|---|---|
| Resectable disease | Surgery (preferred) or Palliative (GAST-9) → GAST-5 |
| Unresectable / Metastatic | Palliative Management (GAST-9) |
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**After Neoadjuvant/Perioperative ICI (MSI-H/dMMR)**

Assessment:
- Chest/abdomen CT with oral/IV contrast (not required if FDG-PET/CT done)
- FDG-PET/CT as clinically indicated (≥5–8 weeks after therapy)
- EGD and biopsy

**Outcomes:**

| Finding | Management |
|---|---|
| No evidence of disease | Observation or Surgery → GAST-5 |
| Persistent local disease | Surgery (preferred) or Palliative |
| New metastatic disease | Palliative (GAST-9) |
:::
::::

# Surgical Outcomes & Postoperative Management {background-color="#1a5276"}

---

## GAST-4: Surgical Outcomes (No Prior Systemic Therapy) {.smaller}

**R0 Resection — Postoperative Management by Tumor Classification**

| Tumor Stage | Management |
|---|---|
| pTis / pT1a N0 / Superficial pT1b | **Observation** → Follow-up (GAST-7) |
| Deep pT1b or pT2, N0 | Observation **OR** Fluoropyrimidine → Fluoropyrimidine-based CRT → Fluoropyrimidine *(selected patients with high-risk features)* |
| pT3, pT4, Any N **OR** Any pT, N+ | **Fluoropyrimidine → CRT → Fluoropyrimidine** if <D2 dissection (category 1) **OR** Chemotherapy if primary D2 dissection (category 1) |

**High-risk features** for pT2, N0 postoperative CRT consideration:
- Poorly differentiated / higher grade cancer
- Lymphovascular invasion (LVI)
- Neural invasion
- Age <50 years
- Did not undergo D2 lymph node dissection

**Other Resection Statuses:**

| Status | Management |
|---|---|
| **R1** | Chemoradiation (fluoropyrimidine-based) |
| **R2** | Chemoradiation OR Palliative Management |
| **pM1** | Palliative Management (GAST-9) |

---

## GAST-5: Surgical Outcomes (Prior Systemic Therapy) {.smaller}

**Patients Who Have Received Systemic Therapy (Perioperative)**

| Resection Status | Postoperative Management |
|---|---|
| **R0** | **Systemic therapy** (category 1) → Follow-up (GAST-7) |
| **R1** | Chemoradiation (fluoropyrimidine-based) **OR** Consider re-resection → Follow-up |
| **R2** | Chemoradiation **OR** Palliative Management |
| **ypM1** | Palliative Management (GAST-9) |

> **ypM1**: The "yp" prefix indicates staging is performed **following** preoperative therapy

---

## GAST-6: Post-Treatment Assessment {.smaller}

**For Unresectable Disease or Nonsurgical Candidates Following Primary Treatment**

**Restaging Modalities:**
- Chest/abdomen/pelvis CT with oral and IV contrast
- CBC and comprehensive chemistry profile
- FDG-PET/CT as clinically indicated (for renal insufficiency or CT contrast allergy)

**Outcomes:**

| Finding | Management |
|---|---|
| **Resectable and medically operable** | Surgery (preferred), if appropriate **OR** Follow-up (GAST-7) |
| **Unresectable or medically inoperable or metastatic** | Palliative Management (GAST-9) |

# Follow-up, Surveillance & Recurrence {background-color="#1a5276"}

---

## GAST-7: Follow-up / Surveillance — Early Disease {.smaller}

**Tis (Successfully Treated by ER)**

- H&P every 3–6 months for 1–2 years, then every 6–12 months for 3–5 years
- CBC and chemistry profile as clinically indicated
- **EGD every 6 months** for 1 year, then **annually for 3 years**
- Routine CT (chest/abdomen/pelvis with contrast) as clinically indicated

**p Stage I — T1a or T1b, N0 (treated by surgical resection or ER)**

- H&P every 3–6 months × 1–2 years; every 6–12 months × 3–5 years
- CBC and chemistry as clinically indicated
- *For patients treated by ER:* EGD every 6 months × 1 year → annually up to 5 years; thereafter as needed
- *For patients treated by surgical resection:* EGD as clinically indicated
- CT chest/abdomen/pelvis with contrast as clinically indicated
- **Monitor for nutritional deficiency** (especially after total gastrectomy); treat as indicated

> After 5 years, additional follow-up may be considered based on risk factors and comorbidities

---

## GAST-7: Follow-up / Surveillance — Advanced Disease {.smaller}

**p Stage II/III or yp Stage I–III (treated with neoadjuvant ± adjuvant therapy)**

- H&P every 3–6 months × 1–2 years; every 6–12 months × 3–5 years
- CBC and chemistry as clinically indicated
- For partial or subtotal gastrectomy patients: **EGD as clinically indicated**
- **CT chest/abdomen/pelvis** with oral and IV contrast every **6 months for first 2 years**, then **annually for up to 5 years**
- Monitor for nutritional deficiency (especially after total gastrectomy)

**Key Nutritional Considerations Post-Gastrectomy:**
Supplement monitoring: Vitamin B12, iron, zinc, calcium, Vitamin D

Consider routine supplementation:
- Daily multivitamin/mineral complex
- Vitamin B12
- Calcium
- Vitamin D

> For **total gastrectomy** patients: surveillance follows above except endoscopy (EGD only if symptomatic)

---

## GAST-8: Recurrence Management {.smaller}

**Locoregional Recurrence**

| Resectability | Management |
|---|---|
| Resectable and medically operable | **Consider surgery** OR Palliative Management (GAST-9) |
| Unresectable or medically inoperable | **Palliative Management (GAST-9)** |

> Surgery should be considered as an option for locoregional recurrence in medically fit patients — review individual cases

**Metastatic Disease**

→ **Palliative Management (GAST-9)**

---

## GAST-9: Palliative Management — Performance Status Pathway {.smaller}

**Unresectable Locally Advanced or Metastatic Disease**

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Good Performance Status**
*(Karnofsky ≥60% or ECOG ≤2)*

1. Perform HER2, CLDN18.2, PD-L1, and MSI testing if not done previously
2. NGS via validated assay
3. Options:
   - **Chemoradiation** (only if locally unresectable and not previously received)
   - **Systemic therapy**
   - Peritoneal carcinoma as only disease → GAST-10
   - **Best supportive care**
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Poor Performance Status**
*(Karnofsky <60% or ECOG ≥3)*

→ **Best supportive care**

---

**When to Re-Test:**
- HER2 testing
- CLDN18.2 testing
- PD-L1 testing
- MSI testing

*(All if not done previously)*

:::
::::

---

## GAST-10: Peritoneal Carcinoma as Only Disease {.smaller}

**Workup (if not done previously):**
H&P, CT chest/abdomen/pelvis, diagnostic laparoscopy, FDG-PET/CT, pathology review

**Treatment Pathway:**

1. **Systemic therapy (GAST-F 4 of 9) for minimum 3 months**

2. **Restaging:** CT scan + diagnostic laparoscopy with washings (PCI ± biopsy) ± FDG-PET/CT ± EGD

3. **Multidisciplinary consultation**

| Finding | Treatment |
|---|---|
| **Low PCI (≤10)**, stable/improved, no metastatic progression, no extraperitoneal disease | If **complete cytoreduction predicted**: Clinical trial or Gastrectomy + cytoreductive surgery + IC/HIPEC or continue systemic therapy |
| **Low PCI (≤10)**, incomplete cytoreduction predicted | Clinical trial or Continue systemic therapy |
| **High PCI (>10)**, progression, or extraperitoneal disease | Systemic therapy, clinical trial, or Best supportive care |

# Principles of Endoscopic Staging and Therapy {background-color="#1a5276"}

---

## Endoscopic Diagnosis (GAST-A) {.smaller}

**Goals of Diagnostic Endoscopy:**
- Determine presence, location, and characteristics of neoplastic disease
- Biopsy all suspicious lesions

**Key Principles:**

- Record tumor location (cardia, fundus, body, antrum, pylorus) and relationship to EGJ (for proximal tumors)
- **6–8 biopsies** using standard-size forceps for adequate material for histologic and molecular interpretation
- Larger forceps may improve diagnostic yield
- EMR or ESD of focal nodules **≤2 cm** can provide better specimens for pathologic assessment (depth, LVI, differentiation)

**EUS for Staging:**
- Provides T-category (depth of invasion), N-assessment, and occasionally M-category
- Hypoechoic (dark) expansion of gastric wall layers identifies tumor location:
  - Layers 1–3 expansion → T1
  - Layers 1–4 expansion → T2
  - Irregular outer border → T3
  - Loss of bright serosal line → T4a
  - Extension to adjacent organs → T4b

---

## EUS Assessment of Lymph Nodes {.smaller}

**Malignant LN Features by EUS:**
- Enlarged
- Hypoechoic (dark)
- Homogeneous
- Well-circumscribed
- Rounded shape

**FNA Indications:**
- Perform if it can be achieved **without traversing** primary tumor or major blood vessels
- Perform if it **impacts treatment decisions**
- Consider FNA to **rule out peritoneal spread** if ascites present

---

## Endoscopic Therapy for Early Gastric Cancer (GAST-A) {.smaller}

**Decision Based on Histology:**

```
Endoscopic Evaluation → Favorable Histology → ER (ESD preferred)
                     → Unfavorable Histology → Gastrectomy (if medically fit)
```

**Favorable Histology:** Well or moderately differentiated

**Unfavorable Histology:** Poorly differentiated or diffuse type

**Curative ER Features:**
- Lesion ≤2 cm
- Superficially invasive: T1a or T1b ≤500 μm
- Well or moderately differentiated
- Complete excision with negative lateral and deep margins
- No LVI

---

## Expanded ESD Indications {.smaller}

**Japanese Gastric Cancer Guidelines and NCCN recognize expanded ESD indications:**

| Criterion | Indication |
|---|---|
| Well/moderately differentiated, **any size**, without ulceration | ESD appropriate |
| Well/moderately differentiated, **sm invasion <500 μm** | ESD appropriate |
| Well/moderately differentiated, **<3 cm with ulceration** | ESD appropriate |
| Poorly differentiated, **<2 cm**, without ulceration | ESD appropriate |

**May be considered curative if:**
- Margins negative
- No LVI
- Curative resection limited to sm1

> Still very small risk of LN involvement → multidisciplinary discussion and patient counseling required

**Incomplete ER Criteria (indicates additional surgery):**
- Poorly differentiated histology
- Evidence of LVI
- Deep submucosal invasion
- Positive lateral or deep margins
- LN metastases

---

## Post-Treatment Endoscopic Surveillance {.smaller}

**Requirements:**
- Careful attention to mucosal surface changes
- **4–6 biopsies** of any visualized abnormalities
- Biopsies of strictures to rule out neoplastic cause

**EUS in Surveillance:**
- High sensitivity for detecting recurrent disease when combined with endoscopy
- **EUS-guided FNA** should be performed if suspicious LNs or wall thickening seen

# Principles of Pathologic Review & Biomarker Testing {background-color="#1a5276"}

---

## Pathologic Review — Specimen Requirements {.smaller}

| Specimen Type | Required Elements in Pathology Report |
|---|---|
| **Biopsy** | Invasion, histologic type, grade; universal MSI/MMR and PD-L1 testing |
| **EMR** | Above + depth of submucosal invasion (μm), vascular/lymphatic invasion, lateral and deep margin status |
| **Gastrectomy** | All EMR elements + EGJ relationship, whether tumor crosses EGJ, LN status, number of LNs recovered (≥16 required) |
| **Gastrectomy after CRT** | All above + assessment of treatment effect; thorough sampling of tumor site if no grossly obvious residual |

> **Minimum 16 regional LNs** should be removed and assessed; **>30 desirable**

---

## Tumor Regression Scoring (Ryan Modified System) {.smaller}

**Post-Chemoradiation Regression Assessment:**

| Score | Description |
|---|---|
| **0 — Complete Response** | No viable cancer cells, including lymph nodes |
| **1 — Near Complete Response** | Single cells or rare small groups of cancer cells |
| **2 — Partial Response** | Residual cancer cells with evident tumor regression, more than single cells or rare small groups |
| **3 — Poor or No Response** | Extensive residual cancer with no evident tumor regression |

**Important Notes:**
- Include lymph nodes in regression score (residual nodal metastases impact survival)
- Acellular mucin pools after CRT should **NOT** be interpreted as residual tumor
- 3-category systems provide good reproducibility among pathologists

---

## HER2 (ERBB2) Assessment {.smaller}

**IHC Scoring Criteria:**

| Score | Surgical Specimen | Biopsy Specimen | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **0** | No/membranous reactivity <10% cells | No/no membranous reactivity in any cell | **Negative** |
| **1+** | Faint reactivity ≥10% cells (partial membrane) | ≥5 cancer cells with faint reactivity | **Negative** |
| **2+** | Weak-moderate complete/basolateral/lateral ≥10% | ≥5 cancer cells with weak-moderate reactivity | **Equivocal** → ISH |
| **3+** | Strong complete/basolateral/lateral ≥10% | ≥5 cancer cells with strong reactivity | **Positive** |

**ISH Criteria for Positivity:**
- ERBB2:CEP17 ratio **≥2**, or
- Average ERBB2 copy number **≥6.0 signals/cell**

> Perform IHC first; ISH only for 2+ (equivocal) results. Positive 3+ or negative 0/1+ results do **not** require ISH.

**HER2 Positivity Rates:**
- EGJ adenocarcinoma: ~32%
- Gastric adenocarcinoma: ~21%
- Intestinal subtype: ~32%
- Diffuse subtype: ~6%

---

## CLDN18.2 Assessment {.smaller}

**Claudin 18 Isoform 2 — IHC Criteria**

| Assessment | Criteria |
|---|---|
| **Positive** | ≥75% viable tumor cells demonstrating moderate to strong membrane CLDN18.2 staining (2+ or 3+ intensity) |
| **Negative** | <75% viable tumor cells demonstrating moderate to strong membrane staining |

**Clinical Relevance:**
- CLDN18.2 is a tight junction protein normally expressed in gastric epithelium; retained during malignant transformation
- CLDN18.2-positive tumors represent **24–38%** of advanced gastric/EGJ adenocarcinomas
- More common in **diffuse subtype**
- Expression is **independent** of dMMR status, HER2 status, and PD-L1

**Testing Indication:** For untreated patients with unresectable locally advanced, recurrent, or metastatic adenocarcinoma when **zolbetuximab** is being considered

---

## MSI/MMR Testing {.smaller}

**Universal Testing Recommended — All Newly Diagnosed Patients**

**Methods:**
- MSI by PCR or NGS (on FFPE tissue)
- MMR by IHC (nuclear expression of MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2)
- Testing should be performed in **CLIA-approved** laboratories
- Patients with MSI-H/dMMR → refer to **genetics counselor**

**MSI Interpretation:**
| Category | PCR Criteria |
|---|---|
| MSS | No instability |
| MSI-Low (MSI-L) | 1%–29% of markers exhibit instability OR 1 of 5 NCI markers |
| **MSI-High (MSI-H)** | ≥30% of markers OR ≥2 of 5 NCI/mononucleotide markers |

**MMR Interpretation:**
| Finding | Interpretation |
|---|---|
| No loss of nuclear expression | No evidence of dMMR (low probability of MSI-H) |
| Loss of nuclear expression ≥1 MMR proteins | **dMMR** |

> MSI-H prevalence in gastric cancer: 19–22%; associated with earlier stage, intestinal subtype, distal stomach, age ≥68

---

## PD-L1 Testing {.smaller}

**Universal Testing — All Newly Diagnosed Patients (candidates for PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors)**

**Key Requirements:**
- Companion diagnostic test on **FFPE** tumor tissue
- **CLIA-approved** laboratory only
- Minimum **100 viable tumor cells** required for adequate evaluation

**Combined Positive Score (CPS):**
$$CPS = \frac{\text{PD-L1 staining cells (tumor + lymphocytes + macrophages)}}{\text{Total viable tumor cells}} \times 100$$

- CPS **≥1** = PD-L1 expression positive

**Tumor Area Positivity (TAP) Score:**
$$TAP = \frac{\text{Area occupied by PD-L1 positive tumor and immune cells}}{\text{Tumor area}} \times 100\%$$

> CPS and TAP score have **high concordance and are interchangeable** for tislelizumab-jsgr and durvalumab

---

## Biomarker Testing Summary {.smaller}

**IHC Testing:**
- HER2 (ERBB2) overexpression
- PD-L1 expression (CPS or TAP)
- MMR protein expression (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2)
- CLDN18.2 expression
- BRAF V600E mutation (VE1)
- TRK A/B/C (NTRK 1/2/3)

**Cytogenetics (ISH):**
- HER2 (ERBB2) amplification (if IHC equivocal)
- NTRK 1/2/3 gene fusions
- RET gene fusion

**Molecular Testing (PCR, NGS):**
- HER2 (ERBB2) amplification
- BRAF codon 600
- MSI testing
- NTRK 1/2/3 gene fusions
- RET gene fusion
- TMB via NGS (CLIA-approved lab)

**Liquid Biopsy (ctDNA):**
- When limited tissue available
- For metastatic/advanced patients unable to undergo traditional biopsy
- Validated NGS-based MGPT in CLIA-approved lab
- Negative result should be interpreted with **caution** (does not exclude tumor)

# Principles of Surgery {background-color="#1a5276"}

---

## Criteria of Unresectability & Siewert Classification {.smaller}

**Criteria of Unresectability for Cure:**

*Locoregionally Advanced:*
- Disease infiltration of root of mesentery or para-aortic LN (highly suspicious or biopsy confirmed)
- Invasion or encasement of major vascular structures *(excluding splenic vessels)*

*Distant:*
- Distant metastasis or peritoneal seeding *(including positive peritoneal cytology)*

> Positive peritoneal cytology in absence of visible peritoneal implants = **pM1 disease**

**Siewert Classification:**

| Type | Definition | Management |
|---|---|---|
| **I** | Epicenter 1–5 cm above EGJ | Esophageal/EGJ guidelines |
| **II** | Epicenter 1 cm above to 2 cm below EGJ | Esophageal/EGJ guidelines |
| **III** | Epicenter 2–5 cm below EGJ, infiltrates EGJ from below | **Gastric cancer guidelines** |

---

## Resectable Tumor Surgery (GAST-C) {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
**Resection Types by Stage:**

- **Tis or T1a** limited to mucosa → candidates for EMR/ESD *(in experienced centers)*
- **T1b–T3** → Adequate resection to achieve negative margins + lymphadenectomy:
  - Distal gastrectomy
  - Subtotal gastrectomy
  - Total gastrectomy
- **T4b** → En bloc resection of involved structures

**Lymphadenectomy:**
- Goal: examine **≥16 regional LNs**
- **D1**: Greater/lesser omenta, perigastric LNs (right/left cardiac, lesser/greater curvature, suprapyloric, infrapyloric)
- **D2**: D1 + LNs along left gastric, common hepatic, celiac, and splenic arteries
- D2 should be performed in **experienced, high-volume centers**
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
**Routine Splenectomy: NOT indicated** unless:
- Spleen involved, or
- Extensive hilar adenopathy

**Minimally Invasive Surgery:**

Criteria for consideration:
- Surgeon experienced in laparoscopic/robotic foregut procedures and lymphadenectomy
- Both early and locally advanced cancers may be considered
- **NOT generally recommended** for T4b or N2 bulky disease

Supported by CLASS-01, CLASS-02, KLASS-01, KLASS-02 trials showing equivalent oncologic outcomes

**Feeding Tube Placement:**
- Consider for select patients undergoing total gastrectomy (especially if postoperative CRT planned)
:::
::::

---

## IC/HIPEC for Peritoneal Disease {.smaller}

**Intraperitoneal Chemotherapy (IC) / Hyperthermic Intraperitoneal Chemotherapy (HIPEC)**

**Evidence Base:**
- Evidence is limited — no definitive randomized trials showing efficacy
- Limited to case reports and small series
- May be effective in **selected patients with low tumor burden**
- Decision requires **multidisciplinary discussion**

**PIPAC:** Pressurized Intraperitoneal Aerosolized Chemotherapy — **investigational only; clinical trial setting**

**Patient Selection for IC/HIPEC:**
1. Pre-treatment: CT chest/abdomen/pelvis + diagnostic laparoscopy (PCI assessment) ± PET
2. Systemic therapy for **minimum 3 months**
3. Restaging: must show stable or improving disease

**IC/HIPEC Criteria:**
- **Low PCI (≤10)**: IC/HIPEC in conjunction with cytoreductive surgery *(complete cytoreduction candidate)*
- **Higher PCI (>10)**: IC/HIPEC only in clinical trial setting
- **Prophylactic IC/HIPEC/PIPAC**: Investigational — clinical trial only

---

## Palliative Surgical Procedures {.smaller}

**Indications:**
- Palliation of symptoms (obstruction or uncontrollable bleeding) when **nonsurgical options are not feasible**
- Does NOT require lymph node dissection

**Options:**

| Situation | Procedure |
|---|---|
| Gastric outlet obstruction (minimal metastatic disease) | **Endoluminal stenting** (preferred) |
| Need for longer-term palliation | **Gastrojejunostomy** (open or laparoscopic) |
| Unresectable disease | Venting gastrostomy and/or feeding tube |

> In incurable disease: surgical resection reserved for symptomatic palliation only when endoscopic/interventional radiology not feasible

# Principles of Multidisciplinary Team Approach {background-color="#1a5276"}

---

## MDT Approach for Esophagogastric Cancers (GAST-E) {.smaller}

**Category 1 evidence supports combined modality therapy** for localized esophagogastric cancer

**Infrastructure Requirements:**

- Joint review of **detailed patient data** on a regular basis (weekly or biweekly meetings)
- All relevant disciplines represented:
  - Surgical oncology, medical oncology, gastroenterology
  - Radiation oncology, radiology, pathology
  - Nutritional services, social workers, nursing
  - Palliative care specialists

**Operational Principles:**

- All long-term strategies best developed **after adequate staging and prior to any therapy**
- Joint review of **actual medical data** more effective than reading reports
- Brief documentation of consensus recommendation for each patient
- MDT recommendations are **advisory** to primary treating physicians
- Re-presentation of outcomes after therapy serves as an educational tool
- Periodic formal review of relevant literature encouraged

# Principles of Systemic Therapy {background-color="#1a5276"}

---

## General Principles of Systemic Therapy (GAST-F) {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
**Regimen Selection Principles:**

- Regimens for esophageal, EGJ, and gastric adenocarcinoma may be **used interchangeably** (except as noted)
- Selection based on: Performance status, comorbidities, toxicity profile
- **Two-drug cytotoxic regimens preferred** for advanced disease (lower toxicity)
- Three cytotoxic drugs: reserved for **medically fit patients with excellent PS** and access to frequent toxicity evaluations

**Key Rules:**

- Trastuzumab: add to first-line chemo for **advanced HER2+ (IHC 3+ or IHC 2+ with ISH/FISH+)** adenocarcinoma
- Checkpoint inhibitor: add to **first-line chemotherapy** for patients with advanced disease **PD-L1 CPS ≥1**
- An FDA-approved **biosimilar** is an appropriate substitute for any biologic

**DPYD Testing:** See NCCN Guidelines for Colon Cancer
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
**Perioperative Systemic Therapy (Category 1):**
- Recommended for localized gastric cancer

**Postoperative Options by Dissection Type:**

| Dissection | Postoperative Therapy |
|---|---|
| **Less than D2** | Chemoradiation |
| **Primary D2** | Chemotherapy (category 1) |

**Subcutaneous Administration:**
- Pembrolizumab + berahyaluronidase alfa-pmph = may substitute IV pembrolizumab *(different dosing)*
- Nivolumab + hyaluronidase-nvhy = may substitute IV nivolumab for monotherapy *(NOT for concurrent IV ipilimumab)*
:::
::::

---

## Perioperative Systemic Therapy Regimens {.smaller}

**Preferred:**
- **FLOT** (Fluorouracil, Leucovorin, Oxaliplatin, Docetaxel) *(category 1)*
- **FLOT + Durvalumab** — *For PD-L1 CPS ≥1 or TAP ≥1%* (category 1); for CPS/TAP <1% (category 2B); for diffuse type (category 2B); for clinical node-negative tumor
- Fluoropyrimidine and oxaliplatin

**Other Recommended:**
- Fluorouracil and cisplatin *(category 1)*

**Neoadjuvant/Perioperative Immunotherapy — Useful in Certain Circumstances (MSI-H/dMMR):**
- Dostarlimab-gxly *(neoadjuvant only)*
- Nivolumab + ipilimumab → nivolumab
- Pembrolizumab
- Tremelimumab + durvalumab *(neoadjuvant only)*

> In MATTERHORN trial: diffuse-type gastric/EGJ adenocarcinoma showed **no EFS advantage** with durvalumab added to FLOT

---

## Postoperative Therapy Regimens {.smaller}

**Postoperative Chemoradiation** *(For patients with <D2 dissection)*

- Fluoropyrimidine (infusional fluorouracil or capecitabine) before and after fluoropyrimidine-based chemoradiation

**Postoperative Chemotherapy** *(For patients with primary D2 dissection)*

Preferred:
- **Capecitabine + oxaliplatin** *(category 1)* — based on CLASSIC trial
- Fluorouracil + oxaliplatin

**Chemoradiation for Unresectable Disease:**

Preferred:
- Fluoropyrimidine alone
- Fluorouracil + oxaliplatin
- Fluorouracil + cisplatin

Other Recommended:
- Fluoropyrimidine + paclitaxel *(category 2B)*

---

## First-Line Therapy — Advanced/Metastatic Disease {.smaller}

**HER2-Positive:**
- Fluoropyrimidine + oxaliplatin + **trastuzumab**
- Fluoropyrimidine + oxaliplatin + trastuzumab + **pembrolizumab** *(CPS ≥1, category 1)*
- Fluoropyrimidine + cisplatin + trastuzumab *(category 1)*
- Fluoropyrimidine + cisplatin + trastuzumab + **pembrolizumab** *(CPS ≥1, category 1)*

**HER2-Negative:**
- + **nivolumab** *(CPS ≥1; category 1 for CPS ≥5)*
- + **pembrolizumab** *(CPS ≥1; category 1 for CPS ≥5)*
- + **tislelizumab-jsgr** *(CPS ≥1; category 1 for CPS ≥5)*
- + **zolbetuximab-clzb** *(CLDN18.2 positive, category 1)*
- Fluoropyrimidine + oxaliplatin *(or cisplatin)*

**MSI-H/dMMR (regardless of PD-L1):**
- Pembrolizumab
- Dostarlimab-gxly
- Nivolumab + ipilimumab
- Fluoropyrimidine + oxaliplatin + nivolumab/pembrolizumab

---

## Second-Line & Subsequent Therapy {.smaller}

**Preferred Regimens:**

| Regimen | Evidence Level |
|---|---|
| **Ramucirumab + paclitaxel** | Category 1 (RAINBOW trial) |
| **Fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki** (HER2+ adenocarcinoma) | **Category 1** (upgraded from 2A) |
| Docetaxel | Category 1 |
| Paclitaxel | Category 1 |
| Irinotecan | Category 1 |
| Fluorouracil + irinotecan | — |
| Trifluridine + tipiracil *(3rd-line or subsequent)* | Category 1 (TAGS trial) |

**Other Recommended:**
- Ramucirumab (monotherapy, category 1)
- Irinotecan ± cisplatin or ramucirumab
- Fluorouracil + irinotecan ± ramucirumab

**Useful in Certain Circumstances:**
- Entrectinib/Larotrectinib/Repotrectinib *(NTRK 1/2/3 gene fusion+)*
- Pembrolizumab or Nivolumab + ipilimumab *(MSI-H/dMMR)*
- Pembrolizumab *(TMB-H ≥10 mut/Mb)*
- Dostarlimab-gxly *(MSI-H/dMMR, no prior ICI)*
- Dabrafenib + trametinib *(BRAF V600E)*
- Selpercatinib *(RET gene fusion+)*

# Principles of Radiation Therapy {background-color="#1a5276"}

---

## Radiation Therapy — General Principles (GAST-G) {.smaller}

**Treatment Recommendations:**
- Must be made after **joint MDT consultation** including: surgical oncologists, radiation oncologists, medical oncologists, radiologists, gastroenterologists, and pathologists
- All available imaging (CT, EUS, FDG-PET, endoscopy reports) should be reviewed prior to simulation

**Simulation and Treatment Planning:**
- **CT simulation** with conformal planning required
- Use **3D-CRT or IMRT**
- Patient instructions: No heavy meal 3 hours before simulation or treatment
- IV and/or oral contrast for CT simulation as appropriate
- **Immobilization device strongly recommended** for reproducibility
- Optimal treatment position: **supine**
- **4D-CT planning** may be used where respiratory motion is significant
- IMRT: carefully define target volumes; account for stomach filling variations and respiratory motion

**Siewert Classification and RT:**
- **Type I & II** → RT guidelines for esophageal/EGJ cancers
- **Type III** → RT guidelines for esophageal/EGJ or gastric cancers depending on tumor bulk location

---

## RT Dose and Target Volume {.smaller}

**RT Dosing:**
- **45–50.4 Gy** (1.8 Gy/day; total 25–28 fractions)
- Higher doses for **positive surgical margins** (boost to that area)

**Target Volume — Postoperative Setting:**
- Use clip placement + pretreatment diagnostic studies to identify tumor bed, anastomosis/stumps, and nodal groups
- Remaining stomach: balance normal tissue morbidity vs. risk of local recurrence
- Coverage of nodal areas modified based on clinical circumstances

**Nodal Areas at Risk by Primary Location:**

| Location | Nodal Areas |
|---|---|
| **Proximal/Cardia/EGJ** | Perigastric, celiac, left gastric, splenic artery/hilar, hepatic artery, porta hepatic; 3–5 cm distal esophagus margin |
| **Middle/Body** | Perigastric, celiac, left gastric, splenic artery/hilar, hepatic, porta hepatic, suprapyloric, subpyloric, pancreaticoduodenal |
| **Distal/Antrum/Pylorus** | Perigastric, left gastric, celiac, hepatic, porta hepatic, suprapyloric, subpyloric, pancreaticoduodenal; 3–5 cm duodenal margin |

---

## Normal Tissue Tolerance Dose Limits {.smaller}

| Organ | Dose Limit |
|---|---|
| **Lungs** | V40Gy ≤10%; V30Gy ≤15%; V20Gy ≤20%; V10Gy ≤40%; V5Gy ≤50%; Mean <20 Gy |
| **Heart** | V30Gy ≤30% (closer to 20% preferred); Mean <30 Gy (closer to 26 Gy preferred) |
| **Spinal Cord** | Max ≤45 Gy |
| **Left / Right Kidney** *(each separately)* | V20Gy ≤33%; Mean <18 Gy |
| **Bowel** | Max dose <54 Gy; V45Gy <195 cc |
| **Liver** | V30Gy ≤33%; Mean <25 Gy |

**Supportive Care During RT:**
- Avoid treatment interruptions; use aggressive supportive care
- Weekly check: vital signs, weight, blood counts
- Prophylactic antiemetics; antacids and antidiarrheals as needed
- If caloric intake <1500 kcal/day → **oral and/or enteral nutrition**
- Feeding J-tube or NG tube may be placed
- Adequate enteral and/or IV hydration throughout CRT and recovery

# Targeted Therapies {background-color="#1a5276"}

---

## Trastuzumab in HER2+ Gastric Cancer {.smaller}

**ToGA Trial (Bang YJ, et al. Lancet 2010):**
- First landmark trial demonstrating benefit of trastuzumab
- Combination with chemotherapy vs. chemotherapy alone in HER2+ advanced gastric/EGJ cancer
- Established HER2 testing as standard

**Key Principles:**
- Add trastuzumab to first-line chemotherapy for advanced HER2+ (IHC 3+ or IHC 2+ with ISH+)
- FDA-approved biosimilar = appropriate substitute
- For advanced/metastatic disease: HER2 testing strongly recommended

---

## Pembrolizumab in Gastric Cancer {.smaller}

**Key Trials:**
- **KEYNOTE-811:** PD-L1 CPS ≥1 HER2+ gastric/EGJ; trastuzumab + chemotherapy ± pembrolizumab → improved OS
- **KEYNOTE-859:** HER2-negative advanced; fluoropyrimidine + oxaliplatin/cisplatin ± pembrolizumab
- **KEYNOTE-062:** Pembrolizumab vs. chemotherapy in first-line advanced/metastatic
- **KEYNOTE-059:** Pembrolizumab monotherapy in previously treated advanced gastric/EGJ cancer

**Indications:**
- First-line: PD-L1 CPS ≥1 (category 1 for CPS ≥5)
- MSI-H/dMMR: pembrolizumab in any line (neoadjuvant, first-line, subsequent)
- TMB-H (≥10 mut/Mb): second-line or subsequent

---

## Nivolumab in Gastric Cancer {.smaller}

**CheckMate 649 (Janjigian YY, et al. Lancet 2021):**
- First-line nivolumab + chemotherapy vs. chemotherapy alone in advanced gastric/GEJ/esophageal adenocarcinoma
- Significant OS improvement, especially in PD-L1 CPS ≥5

**NEONIPIGA Phase II Trial:**
- Neoadjuvant nivolumab + ipilimumab → adjuvant nivolumab in locally advanced MSI-H/dMMR gastric/EGJ cancer
- ~59% pathologic CR rate in 32 patients
- 97% with survival benefit

**Current Indications:**
- First-line: HER2-negative, PD-L1 CPS ≥1 (category 1 for CPS ≥5)
- Neoadjuvant/perioperative MSI-H/dMMR: nivolumab + ipilimumab → nivolumab

---

## Zolbetuximab-clzb (CLDN18.2 Inhibitor) {.smaller}

**Mechanism:** Targets CLDN18.2 tight junction protein exposed during malignant transformation

**SPOTLIGHT Trial (Shitara K, et al. Lancet 2023):**
- Zolbetuximab + mFOLFOX6 vs. placebo in CLDN18.2+, HER2-negative gastric/EGJ adenocarcinoma
- Statistically significant improvement in PFS and OS

**GLOW Trial (Shah MA, et al. Nat Med 2023):**
- Zolbetuximab + CAPOX vs. placebo in CLDN18.2+, HER2-negative gastric/EGJ adenocarcinoma
- Significant improvement in PFS and OS

**Current Recommendation:** Category 1, preferred in first-line for CLDN18.2-positive, HER2-negative disease

---

## Ramucirumab (VEGFR-2 Antibody) {.smaller}

**RAINBOW Trial (Wilke H, et al. Lancet Oncol 2014):**
- Ramucirumab + paclitaxel vs. placebo + paclitaxel in second-line advanced gastric/EGJ adenocarcinoma
- **Category 1, preferred** second-line option

**REGARD Trial (Fuchs CS, et al. Lancet 2014):**
- Ramucirumab monotherapy vs. placebo in second-line setting
- Category 1; "Other Recommended"

---

## Fam-Trastuzumab Deruxtecan-nxki (T-DXd) {.smaller}

**DESTINY-Gastric01 (Shitara K, et al. NEJM 2020):**
- T-DXd vs. physician's choice chemotherapy in previously treated HER2+ gastric/EGJ adenocarcinoma
- Significantly higher ORR and improved OS

**DESTINY-Gastric04 (Shitara K, et al. NEJM 2025):**
- Confirmatory results in second-line HER2+ gastric cancer

**Current Status:** Upgraded to **Category 1** (from 2A) for second-line or subsequent therapy in HER2+ adenocarcinoma

---

## Other Targeted Therapies {.smaller}

| Drug | Target | Indication |
|---|---|---|
| **Tislelizumab-jsgr** | PD-L1 | First-line, CPS ≥1 (category 1 for CPS ≥5); RATIONALE-305 trial |
| **Dostarlimab-gxly** | PD-1 | MSI-H/dMMR neoadjuvant; MSI-H/dMMR subsequent therapy (no prior ICI) |
| **Entrectinib** | NTRK / ROS1 | NTRK 1/2/3 gene fusion+ tumors |
| **Larotrectinib** | NTRK | NTRK 1/2/3 gene fusion+ tumors |
| **Repotrectinib** | NTRK (including after prior NTRK therapy) | NTRK 1/2/3 gene fusion+ tumors |
| **Dabrafenib + Trametinib** | BRAF V600E / MEK | BRAF V600E-mutated tumors (NCI-MATCH trial) |
| **Selpercatinib** | RET | RET gene fusion+ solid tumors (LIBRETTO-001 trial) |
| **Trifluridine/Tipiracil** | DNA polymerase | 3rd-line or subsequent; TAGS trial (category 1) |

# Principles of Surveillance {background-color="#1a5276"}

---

## Principles of Surveillance (GAST-H) {.smaller}

**H. pylori Eradication:**
- All H. pylori-positive patients who underwent curative ER or subtotal resection **must receive eradication regimen**
- Follow latest American College of Gastroenterology or Maastricht consensus guidelines

**Surveillance Evidence Base:**
- Recommendations based on retrospectively analyzed literature and expert consensus
- Sparse prospective data for evidence-based algorithms

**Recurrence Timing:**
- 70–80% of recurrences occur within **first 2 years**
- ~90% of recurrences occur by **5 years**
- ~7.6% of recurrences documented **>5 years** after treatment

> After 5 years, additional follow-up may be considered based on **risk factors and comorbidities**

**Important Prognosis Factors:**
- Stage, depth of invasion, LN status (≥80% of patients have regional LN involvement)
- Positive peritoneal cytology = independent predictor of recurrence
- Alkaline phosphatase ≥100 U/L = marker of poor outcome

# Principles of Survivorship {background-color="#1a5276"}

---

## Survivorship: Long-Term Sequelae Management (GAST-I) {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**General Sequelae:**
- **Weight loss:** Monitor regularly; encourage frequent small meals; dietician referral
- **Diarrhea:** Antidiarrheal agents, bulk-forming agents, dietary manipulation
- **Chemotherapy-induced neuropathy:**
  - Duloxetine for painful neuropathy only (not for numbness/tingling)
  - Referral to OT/PT if fall risk
- **Fatigue:** Physical activity; energy conservation; evaluate psychosocial factors
- **Bone health:** Regular screening; Vitamin D testing and replacement
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Post-Gastrectomy Specific Issues:**
- **Postprandial fullness:** Small, frequent portions; avoid fluid with meals
- **Dumping syndrome:**
  - *Early* (within 30 min): palpitations, diarrhea, nausea, cramps
  - *Late* (2–3 hours): dizziness, hunger, cold sweats, faintness
  - High protein/fiber, low simple carbohydrate diet
- **Vitamin B12 deficiency:** Supplement; monitor ≥every 6 months if not on parenteral B12
- **Iron deficiency:** Monitor CBC and iron annually; supplement orally or IV
- **Small intestinal bacterial overgrowth:** Rifaximin 550 mg TID × 7–10 days
:::
::::

---

## Survivorship: Nutritional Supplementation {.smaller}

**Micronutrient Deficiency Management:**

Supplement with **daily multivitamin/mineral complex** including:
Vitamins A, C, E, D, folate, thiamine, magnesium, zinc, selenium, copper, and iron

**Vitamin D and Calcium:**
- Supplement Vitamin D (follow local practice for dose and monitoring)
- Ensure adequate calcium intake

**Osteopenia/Osteoporosis:**
- Consider bone density testing at **3 years post-gastrectomy**
- Screen for post-menopausal patients or those >50 years of age

> **Subtotal gastrectomy patients**: at decreased risk of nutritional deficiencies — individualize monitoring protocol

---

## Survivorship: Health Behavior Counseling {.smaller}

**Lifestyle Recommendations:**

- Maintain **healthy body weight** throughout life
- **Physically active lifestyle**: minimum 30 minutes moderate-intensity activity most days
  *(Modify for neuropathy or other treatment sequelae)*
- **Healthy diet**: emphasis on plant sources; modify for dumping syndrome or bowel dysfunction
- **Limit alcohol** consumption
- **Smoking cessation** (see NCCN Guidelines for Smoking Cessation)

**Cancer Screening (Average-Risk Survivors):**
- Breast Cancer: NCCN Guidelines for Breast Cancer Screening
- Colorectal Cancer: NCCN Guidelines for Colorectal Cancer Screening
- Prostate Cancer: NCCN Guidelines for Prostate Cancer Early Detection
- Lung Cancer: NCCN Guidelines for Lung Cancer Screening

**Survivorship Care Planning:**
- Maintain therapeutic relationship with **primary care physician (PCP)** throughout life
- Define roles between oncologists and PCP in survivorship care
- Include: treatment history, follow-up surveillance, late effects information, healthy behavior recommendations

# Principles of Palliative Care {background-color="#1a5276"}

---

## Goals of Palliative Care (GAST-J) {.smaller}

> The goal of best supportive care is to **prevent and relieve suffering** and support the best possible quality of life for patients and families, regardless of stage or need for other therapies.

**For gastric cancer, interventions to relieve major symptoms may prolong life** — particularly with multimodality interdisciplinary approach.

---

## Palliative Management: Bleeding {.smaller}

**Acute Bleeding (Hematemesis or Melena):**
→ Prompt **endoscopic assessment**

**Endoscopic Treatment Options:**
- Injection therapy
- Mechanical therapy (endoscopic clips)
- Ablative therapy (argon plasma coagulation)
- Combination methods

*Note: Endoscopic therapies may initially be effective but rate of recurrent bleeding is very high*

**Interventional Radiology:**
- Angiographic embolization when endoscopy is not helpful or bleeding recurs

**Other Options:**
- Palliative gastrectomy in select patients

**Chronic Blood Loss:**
- Proton pump inhibitors (limited data)
- **External beam radiation therapy (EBRT)** — effective for acute and chronic GI bleeding

---

## Palliative Management: Obstruction & Pain {.smaller}

**Malignant Gastric Obstruction:**

*Goals:* Reduce nausea/vomiting; allow resumption of oral diet when possible

| Approach | Options |
|---|---|
| **Endoscopic** | Enteral stent (outlet obstruction); esophageal stent (EGJ/cardia obstruction) |
| **Surgical** | Gastrojejunostomy; gastrectomy in select patients |
| **Radiation** | EBRT |
| **Chemotherapy** | Systemic therapy |

*If obstruction cannot be alleviated:* Venting gastrostomy (percutaneous, endoscopic, surgical, or IR placement)

*For nutritional support:*
- EGJ/gastric cardia obstruction → feeding **gastrostomy**
- Mid and distal gastric obstruction → feeding **jejunal tube**

*Drain ascites before gastrostomy tube placement to reduce infectious complications*

**Pain:**
- EBRT
- Chemotherapy
- NCCN Guidelines for Adult Cancer Pain
- Stent-related severe pain → endoscopic stent removal

**Nausea/Vomiting:**
- NCCN Guidelines for Antiemesis
- Evaluate for luminal obstruction

# NCCN Categories of Evidence & Preference {background-color="#1a5276"}

---

## Categories of Evidence and Consensus {.smaller}

| Category | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Category 1** | High-level evidence (≥1 randomized phase 3 trial or high-quality meta-analysis); **uniform NCCN consensus (≥85% support)** that intervention is appropriate |
| **Category 2A** | Lower-level evidence; **uniform NCCN consensus (≥85% support)** that intervention is appropriate |
| **Category 2B** | Lower-level evidence; **NCCN consensus (≥50% but <85% support)** that intervention is appropriate |
| **Category 3** | Any level of evidence; **major NCCN disagreement** that intervention is appropriate |

> **All recommendations are category 2A unless otherwise indicated**

---

## Categories of Preference {.smaller}

| Category | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Preferred** | Based on superior efficacy, safety, and evidence; and when appropriate, affordability |
| **Other Recommended** | Interventions that may be somewhat less efficacious, more toxic, or based on less mature data; or significantly less affordable for similar outcomes |
| **Useful in Certain Circumstances** | Other interventions that may be used for selected patient populations (defined with recommendation) |

> **All recommendations are considered appropriate**

# Summary {background-color="#003366"}

---

## Key Clinical Decision Points {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**At Diagnosis — Universal Testing:**
1. MSI/MMR status (PCR/NGS or IHC)
2. PD-L1 (CPS, TAP)
3. HER2 if advanced/metastatic
4. CLDN18.2 if advanced/metastatic
5. Consider NGS

**Early Gastric Cancer:**
- EMR/ESD for Tis, T1a, and carefully selected T1b
- Curative criteria: ≤2 cm, ≤500 μm submucosal invasion, no LVI, negative margins
- Surgery if unfavorable histology or incomplete ER

**Resectable Locoregional:**
- Perioperative systemic therapy (FLOT, category 1)
- Consider durvalumab addition if CPS/TAP ≥1%
- MSI-H/dMMR: consider neoadjuvant ICI
- D2 dissection at high-volume centers
- Post-op therapy based on dissection type and residual disease
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Advanced/Metastatic:**
- HER2+ → add trastuzumab (± pembrolizumab)
- HER2-negative, CPS ≥1 → add checkpoint inhibitor
- CLDN18.2+ → add zolbetuximab-clzb
- MSI-H/dMMR → pembrolizumab/dostarlimab/dual ICI

**Second-Line:**
- Ramucirumab + paclitaxel (preferred)
- T-DXd for HER2+ (category 1, upgraded)
- Targeted therapy based on molecular profile

**Surveillance:**
- Stage-based, up to 5 years
- Nutritional monitoring lifelong after gastrectomy
- H. pylori eradication after ER or partial gastrectomy
:::
::::
